Prevention: Avoid planting in areas with a history of head smut because the spores survive in the soil for a long time
Plough deep to bury surviving spores
Plant clean and disease-free maize seeds because the disease can be seed borne
Plant early at the onset of the rains to encourage crop establishment
Avoid feeding livestock with infected materials because it can be transmitted through manure
Use recommended rates of nitrogen fertilizer (100kg calcium ammonia nitrate) per acre.
The disease is more severe in unfertile soils
Monitoring: Begin monitoring just before tasselling because plants are infected systemically and the disease only becomes visible at flowering or ear formation
Abnormal/ malformed tassels before the spores open.
Masses of black spores in the tassels and ears
Take action as soon as one infected plant is observed
Direct Control: Destroy the infected plants by burning or burying away from the maize farm
